r: Stakes, covered pit and tin can wire: uses, rearming, effect on the action screen and in the night attack.
x: Traps are base furniture that you place on the ground, inside the walls or in the yard (up to 15 m from the edge). They work in two ways: on the action screen , when a zombie steps on them, and in the night attack , catching some of the attackers before they reach the walls. Summary Trap Recipe Cost Uses Rearm Effect on the zombie In the night attack Stakes M08 (no workbench, Carpentry, 20 XP) 2 planks , 4 nails 6 1 plank + 2 nails 12 damage and 12 leg damage; can turn it into a crawler Catches attackers (spends uses) Covered pit M10 (no workbench) 2 planks, 2 cloth rags 3 1 plank + 2 rags Falls and stays down ~16 s Catches attackers (spends uses) Tin can wire M09 (no workbench) 1 wire , 2 empty bottles , 2 nails never runs out not needed Rattling cans and a "cans!" alert Hits 15% weaker Stakes A row of stakes measuring 1.2 × 0.6 m. When a zombie walks over it: it takes 12 damage ( "stakes!" appears) and adds 12 to its accumulated leg damage; if the leg damage goes over 60% of its max health, it becomes a crawler ; if its health reaches 0, it dies right there; it spends 1 of the 6 uses. Rearm: walk up to it and tap USE STAKES . It costs 1 plank + 2 nails (from the backpack or the chests), goes back to 6 uses and gives 6 Carpentry XP. Already full: "Already set (6 times)." Covered pit A 1 × 1 m pit disguised with planks and cloth. A zombie that steps on it falls ( "fell into the pit" ) and stays down for triple the normal fall time plus the time to get up: 5 × 3 + 1.2 = 16.2 seconds without attacking. It spends 1 of the 3 uses. Rearm: USE COVERED PIT . It costs 1 plank + 2 cloth rags, goes back to 3 uses and gives 6 Carpentry XP. Tin can wire A low 1.6 m wire with cans hanging from it. When a zombie passes, the cans rattle and "cans!" appears above it: you hear that someone has arrived. It never runs out and doesn't need rearming ( "The can alarm doesn't need anything." ). USE TIN CAN WIRE only explains: "Tin can wire: when a zombie passes, the cans rattle and you hear it." Rules on the action screen A zombie triggers the trap when it enters the trap's area. After triggering a trap, the same zombie can't trigger another for 3 seconds . Uses spent on the action screen stay spent at the base (even when the scene restarts while roaming freely). Rules in the night attack In the night attack and when the horde passes, traps act before the walls: The game goes through each placed stake and pit that still has uses. Each one catches up to one third of the attackers not yet caught (integer division), limited to the uses it has. The uses for those caught are spent. Only the ones left over hit the walls, doors and windows. Example: 9 attackers, a full pit (3 uses) and full stakes (6 uses). The pit catches ⌊9 ÷ 3⌋ = 3 (left with 0 uses); the stakes catch ⌊6 ÷ 3⌋ = 2 (left with 4). That leaves 4 zombies hitting. The tin can wire doesn't catch anyone, but if at least one is placed, each hit of the attack is multiplied by 0.85 (you were warned). The same goes for the watchtower (×0.85) and for a lit floodlight (×0.8); the three multiply together. The attack notice shows how many fell into the traps ( "..., 5 in the traps." ). The base panel reminds you: "Traps catch some zombies in the attack." Tip Put stakes and pits where the zombies will pass: in front of doors and windows and along the yard paths. Rearm after every night: a trap with no uses left catches no one in the next attack. See also Base furniture Night attack Walls, doors and windows

x: Throwing things is for distraction : the noise pulls zombies away from you, and on the action screen the firework stuns and the Molotov burns. There are five throwable items. The items Item Weight Rarity On the map On the action screen Molotov cocktail 0.9 kg uncommon can't be thrown fire on the ground with a 2.4 m radius for 9 s; 25 m of noise Firework 0.3 kg uncommon calls everything within 120 m stuns anyone within 3 m and draws those within 60 m Alarm clock 0.3 kg common calls anyone within 60 m rings for 30 s; every 2 s it draws anyone within 35 m Empty bottle 0.3 kg common breaking glass: 30 m draws anyone within 20 m Rock 0.4 kg common short noise: 18 m draws anyone within 12 m The Molotov is made without a workbench: 3 bottles , 1 gas can and 3 rags make 3 Molotovs. On the map The ball button appears when you have an alarm clock, firework, bottle or rock. With more than one type, it opens the list so you can choose. The item lands 18 m + 1.5 m per Strength level in front of you (where your character is facing). If there is a wall before that, it lands 1 m short of it; never less than 3 m away. Every zombie within the item's radius that wasn't chasing you wakes up, forgets what it was doing and goes to the landing spot. There it searches for 8 s. The landing spot is marked on the map. Each throw gives 3 Stealth experience. Messages: "The firework went off N m away. The whole neighborhood will come see what it was.", "The alarm clock is ringing N m away. They'll go there.", "Bottle smashed N m away. Anyone nearby will see.", "Rock landed N m away." On the action screen You can only throw what is in your pockets . Anything at the bottom of the backpack has to be dug out first (2.5 s; see Backpack and weight ). The button sits next to CROUCH , with the name ( MOLOTOV , FIREWORK , WATCH , BOTTLE , ROCK ) and how many are left. Tap to throw; hold to switch to the next type. If you haven't picked one, the button starts in this order: Molotov, firework, alarm clock, bottle, rock. The item lands 9 m in front of you (14 m at most). If there is a wall in the way, it lands before it. You can't throw at the ground. How zombies react to a distraction An unaware zombie within the radius goes to the spot of the noise. An alert zombie within the radius loses you and goes to the noise if: it is more than 6 m from you, it isn't grabbing you or in the middle of an attack, and it doesn't have you in sight with a clear line. Firework It goes off where it lands ("BOOM!"). Anyone within 3 m is thrown away from the blast (2.5 m/s for 0.6 s) and has a 50% chance of falling. Afterwards it draws anyone within 60 m. Alarm clock It keeps ringing for 30 s ("brrring"). Every 2 s, the ringing draws the zombies within 35 m again. Good for holding a group away while you rummage. r: The formula for the nightly siege on your base: timing, number of attackers, traps, damage, chest losses and the weekly horde.
x: Every night your base suffers a night attack : a group of zombies pounds on the walls, doors and windows. The attack happens even with the app closed and is resolved when you come back. The base panel warns: "Every night (1 AM) the base gets attacked. Sleeping inside it helps defend." When it happens Each night is resolved at 1 AM (phone time). With the app closed, missed nights are resolved when the game runs again: at most 3 nights are applied; any beyond that are skipped. New base: the count starts the following night. It only happens if the base has at least one wall built or just marked out. A base made only of building walls is not attacked. Group base : each night counts only once for everyone; the server picks one phone to apply it and the result reaches the others. How many attack Regular attack: attackers = 2 + random roll from 0 to (2 + M) + 3 if the campfire is lit where M = meters of built wall ÷ 10, rounded. Building walls don't count (they don't fall). Then: +2 if it is night and the floodlight is on (the light draws them). Built walls M Attackers (no fire or light) 0 to 4 m 0 2 to 4 20 m 2 2 to 6 30 m 3 2 to 7 50 m 5 2 to 9 The campfire and floodlight are checked at the moment the attack is resolved. Traps first Before any blow lands, each stake and each covered pit with uses left catches up to a third of the attackers not yet caught (integer division), spending one use per zombie. Caught zombies don't strike. Damage per blow Each remaining attacker lands one blow : damage = (8 + random roll from 0 to 12) × warned × defended Multiplier Condition Value Cans At least one tin can wire placed × 0.85 Tower Watchtower placed × 0.85 Light Night and floodlight on × 0.8 Defended Session open and you at the base by GPS at the moment of the attack × 0.5 Window Blow that landed on a window × 1.3 With everything combined (cans, tower, light and defending), a blow does 2.3 to 5.8 damage instead of 8 to 20. Where each blow lands If there is any door or window that is closed and intact , there is a 35% chance the blow goes to one of them (picked at random). A window takes 30% more. Otherwise, the blow goes to a random built wall (building walls never take blows). A wall already knocked down can also be picked. With no built wall at all, the blow is lost. Walls and openings never go below 0. At 0 health, the wall falls and the door or window becomes a hole. Chest losses After the blows, the game counts the open points: open = knocked-down walls + walls only marked out + open doors + broken doors and windows If there is at least one open point, for each item type in the chests (except clothes): 20% chance the type is hit; if it is, half of that item disappears (rounded up). A base that is closed at the end of the attack loses nothing. The notice sums it all up, for example: "Night attack on the base: 7 zombie(s) (you defended), 2 in the traps. 1 wall(s) down/door(s) open: 3 item type(s) vanished from the chests!" or "... The walls held." Door open at 1 AM Leaving the door open counts as a wall on the ground: even if no wall falls, the chests are exposed. Close the doors before ending the session. The weekly horde passing the base Every week a horde of 30 to 60 zombies crosses your region in a straight line (Wednesday to Sunday, between 7 PM and 10 PM, for 2 h). When the pack passes the point on the route closest to your base: if the route passes more than 300 m from the center of the base, nothing happens; if it passes within 300 m, the base suffers an attack with n = horde size × (1 − distance ÷ 400) , rounded, at least 6 and at most the horde size. This attack follows the same rules as the night attack (traps, damage per blow, multipliers, defense and losses), with two differences: the number of attackers is the horde's (the campfire doesn't add) and a lit floodlight still adds +2. Each horde hits the base only once (on a group base, once for everyone). The notice starts with "The horde passed through the base: ..." . Example:

r: Every noise source in the game, with values, and the math behind the radius in which zombies hear you.
x: Zombies hear as well as they see. On the map, everything you do has a noise level from 0 (silence) to 1 (maximum), and that level becomes a radius in meters: anyone inside the radius hears you. On the action screen noise is measured directly in meters. This page lists every source. The radius math on the map Hearing radius = noise × 120 m (120 m is the noise of a car). Then: Factor Effect on the radius Rain ×0.7 Storm (the thunder muffles footsteps) ×0.6 On the zombie's side, the radius changes further: Zombie Radius it uses Awake (wandering, or dormant that has already woken up) the full radius Dormant that hasn't noticed anything yet half Downed, lying down 30% Any of them, in the small hours (night before 5 AM) ×1.3 What happens when it hears you: within 8 m : it comes after you immediately; within 100 m (or if it was already heading toward another sound): it wakes up and goes to the spot where it heard you. Once there (within 8 m), it searches for 8 s and, if it is dormant or downed, goes back to "sleep". The noise level doesn't change all at once: every half second it moves 60% of the way when rising and only 15% when falling. Running for a bit leaves a noise "trail" for a few seconds after you stop. The meter at the top of the map shows the current radius. Load Source Extra noise Heavy load (pockets or backpack over the limit) +0.03 (about 3.6 m) Expedition pack worn (it rattles) +0.015 (about 1.8 m) See Backpack and weight . Looting on the map With a loot screen open, the noise is at least 0.02 (2.4 m). While you rummage through a piece of furniture, it rises to that furniture's noise, from 0.02 to 0.25 (2.4 to 30 m). The Clumsy trait multiplies furniture noise by 1.5. The full furniture table is in Looting . The game sums up each piece of furniture as: silent : below 0.10 (less than 12 m); moderate noise : from 0.10 to 0.17 (12 to 20 m); loud noise : 0.18 or more (21.6 m or more). r: How to mark out, raise, expand, defend and abandon your base, alone or in a group.
x: The base is a closed polygon that you mark out on the real map. Each side of the polygon is a wall: either a wall you raise with planks and nails (it has health and can fall in the night attack ), or the wall of a real building (free and indestructible). Inside it go the furniture , the chests, the garden and the kitchen . You only have one base at a time. The base menu is under the Base icon on the map, with the BASE tab (walls, outposts, rest, garden, abandon) and the CHESTS tab (all chests together). Privacy notice The first time you tap Mark out base , the game shows the notice "Your base is visible" : in the online game, your base's area shows up for anyone who passes nearby (without your name). The game explicitly asks you not to build your base where you live . To play from home, the game's own recommendation is to set up an outpost there: only you see outposts, and from them you go to the base through the action screen. The notice appears only once (buttons Cancel and Got it ). What others see Other survivors within 300 m receive your base's layout from the server: the walls (health and whether they're raised), the doors and windows, and the placed furniture. Never your nickname, and never what's in the chests. Marking out the base Start the session (you can't mark out without a session: the button shows as Mark out base (start the session) ). Open Base and tap Mark out base . A 1 m grid appears on the map. Tap the grid to place the corners. Each corner must be within 60 m of you . Tap the 1st corner (less than 1.5 m from it) or the Mark out base button on the bar to close it. Use Undo point to remove the last corner and Cancel to give up. Then raise each wall with planks and nails (see below). Marking out is free : the area becomes yours the moment it closes. The build bar shows how many corners you've placed, the current area against the limit, and how many planks and nails the walls will cost. Grid rules The grid has 1 m squares and is aligned with the nearest building (the building's corner within 40 m is a grid node). With no building nearby, it follows north. Only right angles : each new corner is pulled onto the same row or column as the previous one. A corner in the same direction as the previous side stretches the wall instead of creating a new corner. Going back over the same wall is refused ( "Don't go back over the same wall." ). Walls can't cross each other, and you can't mark the same corner twice. When closing, if the last corner isn't aligned with the first, the game adds the missing "elbow" on its own. Corners in the middle of a straight line are removed. If it can't be closed at a right angle, you get "Can't close at a right angle from here. Undo a corner." At least 3 corners are needed. Building walls A whole side lying against a building's wall (every point of the side within 1.5 m of the building's wall) becomes a building wall : it costs no material, starts out "raised", has no health and never falls . The build bar reminds you: "Hug the buildings: building walls are free." A base with only building walls is already closed the moment it's marked out. You can't open a door or window in a building wall, nor push it to expand. Area: limit and growth Source Area New base (free) 50 m² Each Base expansion kit used +10 m² (forever) Each group member beyond the first +15 m² Minimum for any base 4 m² Formula: limit = 50 + 10 × kits + 15 × (group members − 1) . A base larger than the limit is refused ( "Too big: X m² (your limit is Y m²). Base expansion kits raise the limit." ). r: The month's military bunkers: where they appear, the basement floors and their themes, safe rooms, darkness and the generator, quarantine, radio, vault door, loot per floor and the monthly reset.
x: Every month, a few squares in the city hide a military bunker . On top it's a building like any other; below, a staircase leads to basement floors that get ever more dangerous, darker and full of dead soldiers, all the way to the vault at the bottom. The bunker is yours alone: no one else sees what you took from inside. Where they appear Each square on the map has a 10% chance of becoming a bunker for the month. The roll is per square and per month: everyone sees the same bunkers. On the map it shows as "Military bunker (square name)", place type Military bunker . Bunkers change at the start of each month. Floors Each bunker has 3 to 6 floors in total, the same for everyone: the ground floor (rolled like a regular building, with the entrance furniture) and 2 to 5 designed basements. The radio in other bunkers shows this total. Basement themes follow depth: the first is always the Garrison and the last is always the Vault . In between come, without repeats and in this order, up to 3 of Logistics, Command, Armory and Laboratory. On the stairs: GO DOWN (basement N) , GO UP (basement N) and, on the first, UP (entrance) . Basement zombies Per floor: 6 + 2 per floor below the first + 0 to 2 at random, spread across the room area (never in the safe room). Plus the plan's specials: 3 locked in the quarantine cells, the ones on the range, the officer in the briefing room, the Brute in the antechamber. Each bunker zombie has a chance of being a soldier of 50% + 12% per floor, at most 85%. The rest are regular . 15% of them are lying down (in the barracks, 50%). The zombies come back every time you leave and re-enter the bunker. Each one's body only yields loot once per month. Safe rooms and return point Every basement starts in a safe room : the stairs up, an armored door (you get through, zombies don't get through or break it), the FLOOR PLAN on the wall and a supply locker with one simple thing (water, bandage, batteries, crackers, gauze or painkiller). The plan shows the floor's rooms and doors, with no zombies or loot. Stepping into a safe room saves your return point there. If the app closes in the middle of the visit, entering the bunker again takes you straight to the last safe room ("Back in the safe room of basement N."). Leaving through the front door clears the return point: the next visit starts from the ground floor. Dying inside also clears it. r: How fatigue rises and falls, its levels and effects, and how much you rest and heal sleeping at the base, in a bed, in a sleeping bag or out on the street.
x: Fatigue goes from 0 to 100% and shows up in the Fatigue bar on the Health tab. It rises as you walk and run and only really drops when you stop or end the session. In Footfall, sleeping is ending the session : the time with the app closed is your sleep time, and where you ended determines how restful it is. The result never goes below 30. Sleeping To sleep, open the menu and tap Sleep (end here) when you're in a safe place, or End session outside one. The game confirms: Sleep at the base? / Sleep at the outpost? with the Sleep button, or End here? with the End button. Ending anywhere keeps everything you're carrying. Safe places to sleep are: inside your base, at one of your outposts or in your pitched tent. "You slept in the sleeping bag: better rest than the ground, but not like a bed." Health : only comes back while sleeping if you're not bleeding or carrying a zombie infection. Mind : sleeping with base rest, stress drops 30 and sadness 5 per hour; with normal rest, 10 and 1 per hour. The column shows the hour multiplier: in a bed each hour counts as 1.5. See Mind . The messages when you end say where you slept: "You slept at the base. Full rest while the app is closed.", "You slept in the tent. ...", "You slept at the outpost. ...". What happens while you sleep Hunger and thirst keep dropping, but stop at 11% (see Needs ). Treated wounds keep healing in real time (without the stretcher bonus). Bleeding doesn't drain health with the app closed, and wounds don't catch common infections. The zombie infection keeps running and can kill you before you come back. Your base can suffer night attacks . How much to sleep At the base without a bed, 8 h closed clears fatigue and restores 40 health. With a bed, just over 5 h already clears fatigue, and 8 h restores 60 health. The bed ("Bed" recipe, 3 planks, 2 nails and 4 rags, at the workbench) is one of the first pieces of furniture worth building.

r: The action screen's three control modes, the screen halves, the FIGHT button, crouching, the target selector and the running threshold.
x: The action screen has three control modes. Choose one in Settings → CONTROLS . The mode also applies in memories. The three modes Mode In-game description Sticks Simple (default) "One stick and the FIGHT button; tap to strike, running leaves the fight" left one moves; FIGHT button on the right Two sticks "Aim with the right stick; tapping the screen strikes and shoves" left one moves; right one aims Automatic "One stick; strikes, shots and shoves on their own" a single one, in the bottom middle The screen halves There is no attack button: the whole screen is the button. A quick tap : on the left half : shove; on the right half : strike (with a firearm, shoot). Holding and dragging the screen moves the camera to see more of one side; Center (at the top) brings it back. Taps don't attack while a panel is open or in the base's build mode. Pressing strike before the weapon is ready delays the next strike by 0.15 s ("too soon!"). Standing still and not aiming, the strike turns by itself toward the nearest zombie within 1.6× the weapon's reach. Simple mode and the FIGHT button The FIGHT button turns on the fighting stance and then shows FIGHTING , in amber. In the stance you automatically face the nearest zombie (with a firearm, the nearest one you can see within 14 m; with a melee weapon, within 2.2× the weapon's reach) and move sideways, at 60% speed. The stance counts as aiming all the time : more accurate strikes with a chance of critical (see Melee combat ). Tapping the screen outside the stance turns the stance on and strikes immediately. Running turns the stance off ("who runs doesn't fight"). It also turns off by itself after 6 s with no zombie within 12 m ("relaxed"). When off, the button pulses red when an alert zombie is within 8 m. Two sticks mode The right stick (red) aims: wherever it points, your character looks and strikes. Holding the right stick turns on the fighting stance while you hold it and for 0.4 s after you let go. With a firearm, the aim you set stays in effect for 1.5 s even while walking (you can strafe while shooting). Striking without aiming (right stick released) is worse: damage ×0.85, a 25% chance of a glancing blow (half damage) and a higher chance of missing the head. Automatic mode You only move. Your character faces the nearest zombie and: strikes by itself when a zombie is within the weapon's reach; shoots by itself when it sees a zombie within 14 m (even with longer-range weapons); shoves by itself when on the ground or grabbed, and when there are 3 or more zombies within 1.1 m (if it has stamina for the shove + 5); the shove hits all around (360°), not just in front. The price: the interval between automatic strikes is 1.35× longer, further multiplied by 1 + panic ÷ 200 (with panic at 100, about 2× normal) and by the reflex rate (Fast reflexes ×0.9, Slow reflexes ×1.1), it hits 15% weaker and has only a 4% base critical chance. Automatic bursts come out shot by shot, at the weapon's rate of fire. Taps on the screen halves also work in this mode. Walking and running Stick Speed Up to 72% of its travel walking, proportional, up to 2.0 m/s Beyond 72% (the edge) running, 4.2 m/s Running needs more than 5 stamina and uses 10 per second (4% less per Stamina level). You can't run while crouched, on the ground or grabbed. Walking uses 2 stamina per second (proportional to the stick). With less than 10 stamina you walk at 70%. While running, any unaware zombie within 5 m (times the footstep multiplier) notices you instantly. Other speed multipliers: load (see Backpack and weight ), pain, fracture, cluttered floor and the Adrenaline junkie trait (+10% with strong panic, +25% at extreme). On the ground, moving the stick makes you get up faster. Crouching The CROUCH button (it becomes STANDING ) is on the left, above the stick. You move at 45% speed and can't run. Unaware zombies only see you within 4.5 m (standing, 7 m) and take twice as long to notice. Shots spread 1 degree less. Armed guards hit less

r: How long bodies stay on the ground, how to search the pile, each zombie's pocket odds, loot from uniformed zombies and the stamp in the pocket.
x: Every zombie you take down leaves a body that can be searched. On the action screen you search each one right there; when the fight ends, the leftover bodies become a pile on the map, which stays on the ground for a while so you can come back and search it. Searching on the action screen Get within 1.3 m of a body: SEARCH BODY (2.0 s) appears. Stand still until it finishes. It makes 4 m of noise. Once searched, the button becomes BODY (n) with the number of items. A body that's been searched and emptied no longer shows up. The time follows the same rule as looting: divided by looting speed (Burglar 1.5×, sad 10% slower). The pile on the map All the bodies from one fight fall into a single pile (one loot screen). If there's already a pile of zombie bodies within 40 m , the new ones join it. The name shows how many there are: "Zombie body" or "N zombie bodies". The pile lasts 2 h from the last body that joined it. It also disappears when everything has been searched and emptied. A body searched on the action screen and emptied doesn't join the pile; one searched with leftovers joins with what's left. Fights inside bunkers and in the arena of strongholds don't leave a pile on the map. With the Loot button (the pile counts from the nearest body, within 35 m), the screen shows all the bodies together: Search all (X s) searches one body after another, without needing to tap again. Each body takes 2.0 s and is quiet (0.03, about 3.6 m). If you stop halfway, the button becomes Search the rest . The items from all searched bodies show up together; Take all takes them all. Noise The screen itself warns you: "Opening makes noise. If a zombie sees you, the fight starts and you leave here." A common zombie's pocket Each body is rolled like this: 45% chance of having cloth rags (the torn clothing). From the pocket: 35% chance of nothing; otherwise 1 item (70%) or 2 items (30%) from the list below. If ammo comes up, it's 1 to 4 rounds. 6% chance of having a stamp (a letter in the pocket). r: How the crow arrives, what it does on the map, feeding it, the 5 bond levels and what each one unlocks.
x: The crow is a companion only you can see. It follows you on the map, warns you about hordes, points out bodies, shows you one place with something rare each day and, once bonded, carries things to and from the radio depot . The Crow button appears on the map during the session after it arrives. Arrival The crow arrives when you put the first door on your base (as in Poe's poem, it perches above the door): "A crow landed on your door. It stays." From then on it's yours. See Walls, doors and windows . What it does on the map The crow flies at 9 m/s on the map. Every 4 seconds it looks around, in this order of priority: Priority Behavior Rule — Flees from noise Gunshot or loud noise: it caws, flies 80 m away and only goes back to doing things after 90 s 1 Horde warning With 6 or more zombies chasing you or heading toward a noise, between 25 and 200 m from you, it comes flying from their direction and caws: "The crow comes cawing from the north: lots of zombies that way." The phone vibrates. At most 1 warning every 10 minutes. It doesn't say how many there are. 2 Unusual zombie (level 3+) Circles over a uniformed zombie you haven't seen yet, between 25 and 90 m: "The crow is circling over something unusual to the east: firefighter." The same zombie is only pointed out again after 5 min. 3 Place of the day Once a day, it flies to a not-yet-looted place between 150 and 400 m away (preferably around 250 m) and perches there for 10 minutes: "The crow landed on (place). There seems to be something rare there." The first time that place is set up, it gets one extra rare item (from the lists for that type of place; with no rare on the list, any rare, never an expansion kit, outpost radio or outfit). 4 Bodies Circles for 25 s over a pile of bodies you haven't searched yet, within 80 m. The same pile only again after 5 min. — Idle Follows from a distance and perches 10–30 m from you now and then (every 40–100 s, or if it gets more than 45 m away) Group messages When a group mate sends a quick alert ( HORDE HERE , LOOT HERE , HELP! ), the crow comes flying from your mate's direction (from up to 150 m away) and caws when it arrives. r: From the PLAY button to the map: safety notice, appearance, profession, traits, starter kit and the opening story.
x: Character creation in Footfall follows the Project Zomboid model: you choose a profession , spend or earn points with traits and start with a basic kit in your backpack. The first time you play, the full path is: safety notice → appearance (step 1 of 2) → profession and traits (step 2 of 2) → invitation to the opening story → map tutorial → map , with the session already starting. Screen order On the start screen, tap PLAY . If the game requires an account (the text below says "Sign in or create an account to play"), the button opens the login; there is also the LOG IN / CREATE ACCOUNT button. While the cloud save loads ("Loading the game from the cloud…"), PLAY is disabled. Safety notice ( BEFORE YOU HEAD OUT ): appears once per phone. You only get past it by tapping GOT IT, LET'S GO . New survivor · 1 of 2 : nickname and appearance. Ends with Continue . New survivor · 2 of 2 : profession and traits. Ends with Start with the basic kit in your backpack . THE LAST DELIVERY : invitation to the short opening story (only appears until you play it or decline it once). Paged map tutorial (first time only) and then the map, with the session starting on its own. Steps 1 and 2 only appear when the account has no character yet and has never had one that died. After a death , the new character is created straight at step 2 ( New survivor button on the death screen, or Create character on the map's "Your survivor died" card); the appearance stays the same. Safety notice The BEFORE YOU HEAD OUT screen lists five rules and cannot be closed with the back button the first time: Never play while driving, cycling or crossing the street. Stop somewhere safe before looking at the screen. Look around, not at the phone: holes, cars, bikes and people are real. The game's places are just map references. Don't enter real houses, shops, lots or buildings. At night, stick to lit, busy streets and tell someone where you are going. Bring water, respect your body and stop if you get tired. The game waits. The acceptance is stored on the phone (not on the account): if you switch devices, it appears again. Afterwards you can review the notice through the Tutorial in Settings. Step 1: nickname and appearance Nickname The Nickname (optional) field can be left empty. If filled in, it must have 3 to 16 characters, only letters (accented allowed), numbers and _ , no spaces. The error messages are "At least 3 letters.", "At most 16 letters." and "Only letters, numbers and _ (no spaces).". The nickname is only shown to your group and can be set later. Appearance You choose three colors, each from five options: Row Options Default Skin 5 tones, from lightest to darkest 2nd tone Hair 5 tones 2nd tone Colored part of the outfit 5 colors 1st color The name of the third row changes with the outfit you're wearing: in the starting outfit, Survivor (scarf, backpack and chest flashlight), it's called Scarf . The outfit itself isn't chosen here: "New outfits are found by exploring; change them at the wardrobe in the radio vault." A preview of the figure shows the result. Your appearance is what sets you apart from other players on the action screen (there's no name above the figure), and it's what shows on the zombie that stands over your belongings when you die . Privacy Step 1 itself warns: other players only see your figure, with no name, and only on the action screen; your base shows up for anyone passing nearby (no name), so don't build where you live (use an outpost at home, which only you see); your location is only used while the session is active. Each card shows the name, the points ( +8 points , -4 points ...) and what it gives: skill levels, free traits and notes. The initially selected profession is Unemployed . r: The 300 kg personal room with workbench, wardrobe, mailbox and shelf; outposts and the tent: limits, distances and costs.
x: The radio vault is a personal room, yours alone, that every outpost and your tent lead to. It holds your 300 kg inventory, a workbench, the wardrobe, a mailbox, the shelf of memories and the radio that takes you to the base. It belongs to the account: it stays yours if you leave a group and when the character dies. How to get there Go to one of your outposts or to your pitched tent (within 25 m of them). The Outpost: radio vault button (or Tent: radio depot ) appears on the map, and it glows when you can go. Tap it: the action screen opens inside the vault room. You disappear from the map while you're there. You can't go if you're in a fight ( "Finish the fight first." ), with a zombie chasing you ( "There's a zombie after you." ) or with a zombie 10 m away or closer ( "A zombie is too close." ). The room A 50 m² square (7.07 m per side). Get within 1.3 m of each thing and tap the button that appears: Object Where Button What it does Vault (big chest) Back wall, on the left VAULT (N/300 kg) Your 300 kg inventory Workbench Back wall, on the right WORKBENCH Workbench recipes using what's in the vault and the backpack (doesn't make base furniture) Radio (on the table) Front wall RADIO: GO TO BASE / RADIO: GROUP BASE Leaves the room and opens the action screen inside the base Wardrobe Left wall WARDROBE / WARDROBE: STORE NEW OUTFIT Stores and wears outfits (see Sewing and clothes ) Mailbox Right wall MAILBOX: MARKET AND STORE Market and store Shelf Left wall, below the wardrobe SHELF OF MEMORIES (N) The memories you've already read, ready to play Away from everything, the hint on screen is "Radio depot: get close to the chest, the workbench, the radio, the wardrobe or the shelf" . In the vault you can't drop things on the floor ( "You can't drop things here: put them in the vault." ), and no other player enters the room. r: The nine wound types, where each hit lands, how much it bleeds, how long it takes to heal, the steps it needs and how clothing protects you.
x: Wounds sit on one of the six body parts and each one needs its own treatment steps. A wound only starts healing when all the steps it needs are done and it isn't infected. Open wounds bleed, hurt, can catch a common infection, and some can pass on the zombie infection . You can see everything in the character panel, Health tab, on the Vitruvian figure (each part gets redder the worse the wound is, and shifts toward green if infected) and on the wound cards below it. Wound types Wound Bleeds (untreated) Heals in Steps it needs Pain Passes zombie infection Scratch 1 HP every 30 s (2/min) 1 day Clean, Bandage 5 7% Laceration 1 HP every 12 s (5/min) 3 days Clean, Bandage 12 25% Bite 1 HP every 15 s (4/min) 5 days Clean, Bandage 15 85% Deep cut 1 HP every 8 s (7.5/min); bandaged without a suture, 1 every 40 s 4 days Clean, Suture, Bandage 15 No Shard 1 HP every 25 s (2.4/min) 2 days Remove the shrapnel, Clean, Bandage 18 with the shard in, 8 without No Hemorrhage 1 HP every 3 s (20/min) 5 days Tourniquet, Clean, Suture, Bandage 20 25% Fracture Doesn't bleed 7 days Immobilize (splint) 32 without a splint, 15 with No Burn Doesn't bleed 3 days Ointment, Bandage 20 without ointment, 8 with No Bruise Doesn't bleed 12 hours None 8 No The zombie infection chances in the table are the normal ones; the immunity traits change these numbers (see Infection ). Healing times are in real time and count from the moment the last step was done; they're multiplied by the healing trait, the First aid level and the base stretcher (see Treatment ). A treated wound stays on the body, hurting half as much, until the healing bar fills. Notes on each type Scratch, laceration and bite : stop bleeding as soon as they're bandaged. Cleaning is only asked for while the wound isn't bandaged: if you bandage first, the game no longer asks for cleaning, but a wound bandaged without cleaning has the highest chance of common infection (see below). Deep cut : bandaging reduces the bleeding but doesn't stop it. Until it's sutured the card shows leaking (needs suture) and you lose 1 HP every 40 s. Shard : the fragment stays inside ( shrapnel inside ) until you take it out. With the fragment inside the wound hurts more and has an extra chance of common infection. Bandaging stops the blood, but it doesn't replace removing the shard. Hemorrhage : only stops bleeding with a tourniquet or a suture; a bandage isn't enough. The tourniquet can stay on for 2 hours at most: after that the limb without blood takes 1 HP every 120 s until you suture it (the suture releases the tourniquet). Fracture : makes you slow on the action screen (speed ×0.65 without a splint, ×0.85 with a splint) and gives the Fracture moodle. Burn : without ointment, it has a 3% chance per hour of catching a common infection. Bruise : this is the hematoma. It needs nothing and goes away on its own in 12 hours. It doesn't tear clothing and never gets infected. x: A group brings together up to 10 survivors. Members see on the panel where each one is and how far away, send quick alerts with their location, chat, trade items side by side and share a base with shared chests. The panel is under the Group icon on the map. Everything in a group requires an online account : with no connection, the panel shows "No connection to the server. Sign in to use the group." and the Log in to account button. Create or join Action How What happens to your base Create Type the New group name (up to 24 letters; empty becomes "Group") and tap Create group If you have a base, it becomes the group's base and the chests are uploaded to the server ( "Group created. Code: ... Your base now belongs to the group." ) Join Type the Group code (6 characters) and tap Join group If you have a base, it is dismantled : chests and materials go to the radio depot and the garden is lost (the game asks for confirmation) You can only be in one group at a time ( "You're already in a group." ). Privacy Your nickname is private : no one sees it on the map or above your character; only your group. Outside the group, others only recognize you by your clothes and colors. The group sees where you are (panel and alerts). Other survivors never see you on the map: they only appear to you, and you to them, on the action screen, when they're close, with no name. No one outside sees names ( "No one outside sees names." ). The panel shows the last 30 messages (the game keeps up to 100), with who sent them and how long ago. Quick alerts appear in the same list, highlighted. x: Skills go up with use, from level 0 to 10 , and are all lost when the character dies ("They go up with use. If you die, you lose it all."). You start with the levels given by your profession and by some traits . Progress appears on the character panel, Skills tab: ten little level squares and a thin bar with the XP to the next one. r: The weekly migrating horde, random alarms, helicopter supply drops and rescue flares, with waves, timings and crates.
x: Besides the zombies that live on each street, the world has events: a horde that crosses the area every week, alarms that go off and pull in the zombies around them, supply drops left by helicopter and rescue flares , which you light to face waves and earn a crate. The horde and the drops are the same for every player in the same area. The area is a square of about 2 km (0.02 degree). Your "location" for events is your base; without a base, wherever you are. The horde on the map The pack's position appears on the map if you have a radio or if you're less than 400 m from it. When the pack passes less than 500 m from you, its zombies actually appear around the point (within 35 m), already awake and walking toward where the pack will be 3 minutes later. They follow the pack; if they hear or see you, they leave it and come after you like any zombie. Uniforms: 6% soldiers, plus 7% street specials (see Zombies ). When the horde ends, those of its members that aren't chasing you disappear. Damage to the base If the route passes less than 300 m from the center of the base, when the pack goes by the closest point the base suffers a horde attack (once per horde, applying to the whole group at the group's base): Attackers = horde size × (1 - distance ÷ 400), between 6 and the total size. At 0 m they all come; at 200 m, half. Traps catch some first: each armed stake or pit catches up to a third of the remaining attackers, using up charges. Each attacker takes 8 to 20 health off a wall or opening. 35% of the blows go to doors and windows (windows take 30% more). With a warning, the damage is lower: tin can alarm ×0.85, watchtower ×0.85, floodlight lit at night ×0.8. If you're at the base with the session open, ×0.5. If any wall fell or any door was left open, each type of item in the chests (except clothing) has a 20% chance of losing half. The summary appears as "The horde passed through the base: N zombie(s)...". r: The zombie infection (stages, 7-day deadline, chance per wound and per trait) and the common wound infection, which antibiotics cure.
x: Footfall has two kinds of infection, which have nothing to do with each other: Zombie infection : comes from wounds caused by zombies. It has no cure and kills in 7 days of real time. Common infection : sets in on a dirty or poorly treated wound . It gets in the way a lot, but an Antibiotic cures it. Zombie infection How you catch it Every wound a zombie causes rolls, on the spot, whether it passes on the infection: Wound Normal Strong immunity Weak immunity Bite 85% 60% 100% Laceration 25% 12.5% 40% Hemorrhage 25% 12.5% 40% Scratch 7% 3.5% 11.2% Any other (bruise, fracture, burn, cut, shard) 0% 0% 0% When clothing stops a bite, it becomes a bruise and doesn't infect. Wounds from guards and from accidents (broken glass, tools, fire) never pass on the zombie infection. Being bitten always shows "You were bitten..." and adds 20 stress and 15 sadness, whether it infects or not. There is only one infection: if you are already infected, another infected wound doesn't change the clock. The deadline counts from the moment of the first wound that infected you. Stages Time since the wound Stage Moodle Effects 0 to 3 days Incubating — No symptoms ("Bitten. No symptoms yet.") 3 to 5 days Fever Feverish (level 2) −25 max stamina; −10% combat damage; stress rises 5 to 7 days Delirium Delirious (level 3) −35 max stamina; map vision ×0.6; −20% combat damage; stress rises 7 days Death — "The infection won." The days are real and keep running with the app closed. If the deadline runs out while you're away, the character dies when you open the game ("The infection won while you were away."). See Death . In the Health tab, while there is an infection, the stage text appears along with "Time left: ... (real time). There's no cure yet.". Other effects While infected, you don't recover health by sleeping (not at the base, not in a bed, not in a sleeping bag). While playing, health keeps coming back at 1 per minute if the other conditions allow it (see Needs ). During fever and delirium, stress rises 0.05 per second with the app open (see Mind ). No item or medicine cures or delays the zombie infection. Antibiotics have no effect on it. How to avoid it Wear protection on your arms and torso, where most bites land (see Wounds ). Leather and rigid pieces stop 85% to 95% of bites where they cover. The Strong immunity trait lowers bites to 60% and cuts the chance from lacerations and scratches in half. A standing zombie only bites after grabbing you (or when you are down on the ground); a crawler bites right away. Break free of a grab quickly and avoid being knocked down. Bitten isn't dead (yet) There's a 15% chance a bite doesn't infect. And even infected you have 7 real days: time to take what matters to the base and the chests, which remain after death. Common infection How you catch it For every hour with an active session , each wound that can bleed (scratch, laceration, bite, deep cut, shard; not hemorrhage) has a chance that is the sum of: Situation Chance per hour Bandaged without being cleaned 6% Dirty dressing (a dressing older than 12 h, 24 h with medical tape, or a rag one) 4% Shard still inside 5% No dressing at all (except scratches) 2% A burn without ointment has 3% per hour, separately. Bruises and fractures never get infected. Example: a laceration bandaged with a rag and not cleaned adds up to 6% + 4% = 10% per hour. The chance is only rolled with the app open, outside the action screen. With the app closed, the wound doesn't get infected. Effects The wound becomes INFECTED and stops healing (even with every step done). Pain +10 on that wound. The Infected wound moodle (level 2) and −15 max stamina. With the app open, health doesn't come back. After 72 h infected, the wound takes 1 HP every 600 s (6 per hour). Cure Take an Antibiotic ( Take in the inventory): it cures the common infection on all wounds at once ("Antibiotic: the wound infection will go away.") and also restores 20 health (plus 10% per First aid level). r: The opening memory and controls tutorial: the mail carrier on the first night.
x: The last delivery is the game's first memory and works as a tutorial . Unlike the others, it is not a book: the game offers it the first time you log in, right after you create your first character, and it is always playable on the shelf at the radio depot . Card Protagonist The mail carrier, on the last round of the day · day 0, 8:10 PM Where to find Offered at the start of the game; afterwards, on the memory shelf (playable even if you haven't finished it) Challenge type Controls tutorial: walking, sneaking, rummaging, fighting, shooting and running; each scene teaches one control Length About six minutes Weather Night, thunderstorm Profession Unemployed, no traits Starting kit 1 Flashlight , 1 Batteries Reward Mail carrier outfit (blue uniform, cap and the mail bag across the shoulder), in the wardrobe at the radio depot Scoreboard Kills (the record stays on the shelf) How to start On your first login, the THE LAST DELIVERY screen invites you: PLAY THE FIRST NIGHT or GO STRAIGHT TO THE CITY (skip; the game won't ask again). Afterwards, play it from the shelf at the radio depot. Playing from the shelf ends your session, because the memory uses a different character. Gameplay tips The flashlight is in the left corner of the screen. It helps you see, but they see you too. Floors are connected by stairs: get close and use GO UP / GO DOWN . Those who haven't seen you yet have a cone on the ground: come up from behind, crouched, for the stealth kill. Rummaging through furniture takes time and makes noise. Stay still until the bar fills. A zombie raising its arm or opening its mouth is about to attack: get out of reach. If grabbed, run in the opposite direction. If you fall too early, choose FROM HERE to continue from where you were. The record is for kills: it's worth coming back to beat it. See also Memories Action screen Tailoring and clothes (outfits)

x: Thursday duty is the memory of a military police officer at the neighborhood police station, on the first day. r: Panic, stress, sadness, boredom, cigarette addiction, phobias and hemophobia: what makes them rise, the levels, the effects and how to bring them down.
x: The survivor's mind, in the style of Project Zomboid, has four meters: panic (the fright of the moment), stress , sadness and boredom . The last three appear as bars in the Head section of the Health tab; panic appears as a moodle. They all go from 0 to 100. Panic Levels Panic Level Moodle 0 to 14 0 — 15 to 34 1 Mild panic 35 to 59 2 Panicked 60 to 79 3 Strong panic 80 to 100 4 Extreme panic Panic from the map carries over to the action screen and comes back to the map at the end of the fight. The levels are the same in both places. What makes it rise On the map : each zombie within 40 m that you can see or that is chasing you adds, per second, 1.5 × (1 − d/40)² (3 × if it's chasing you), where d is the distance. The closer they are and the more zombies there are, the faster it rises. Inside a closed base (walls standing and doors shut), zombies don't cause panic. On the action screen : Cause Panic A zombie that noticed you within 10 m, seen or sensed 10 × (1 − d/10)² per second, added per zombie A zombie that suddenly appears less than 6 m away up to +8 from the scare Taking damage +6 Being grabbed +10 Being knocked down +15 Getting wounded, with Hemophobic +12 Cigarette withdrawal +10 at the start of the fight Every panic gain (except the one from withdrawal) is multiplied by: Factor Multiplier Brave / Cowardly / Desensitized ×0.3 / ×2 / ×0 Stress ×(1 + stress/133): 75 stress = +56% Anti-anxiety pills ×0.4 Beta blocker ×0.5 Cachaça (drank less than 1 h ago) ×0.4 Days alive (getting used to it) from ×1 on day 1 to ×0.4 at 60 days or more How to bring it down With no zombie nearby, panic drops on its own: 1.5 per second on the map and 2.5 per second on the action screen, multiplied by how used to it you are (from ×1 on the first day up to ×3 at 60 days alive). On the action screen, each shove takes off 10. Items: Item Panic Bottle of cachaça Clears it Anti-anxiety pills −40 Pack of cigarettes (Smoker only) −20 Beta blocker −15 Effects Map : the vision cone narrows 0.25° per point of panic (down to −25°). Action screen, vision : the cone narrows 0.5° per point (never below 110°). Melee attack (see Melee combat ): −10% damage at Panicked, −20% at Strong panic, −30% at Extreme panic; the critical window shrinks and the critical chance drops; the chance of missing the head goes up. Shove : pushes and knocks down less (−8% force and −10% knockdown chance per level). Shooting : spread grows with panic; below Firearms 6, Strong panic takes off 15% and Extreme panic 25% of the damage. Treatment : sutures and shard removal fail 8% more at Panicked, 16% at Strong panic, 24% at Extreme panic (see Treatment ). Adrenaline junkie : the trait turns high panic into an advantage: +10% speed at Strong panic and +25% at Extreme panic. Phobias The Claustrophobic and Agoraphobic traits create a panic floor of 35 in certain places: Phobia Where Claustrophobic With 4 or more buildings within 15 m of you (alleys, closed blocks) Agoraphobic When the nearest street (within 15 m) is wide, 9 m or more (avenues and main streets) On the map, in these places panic doesn't drop below half the floor (17.5, Mild panic). On an action screen opened there, panic rises on its own up to 35 (Panicked) even with no zombie. Desensitized has no phobias. Hemophobia With the Hemophobic trait: each treatment step done in the Health tab adds +10 panic; the quick dressing adds +35; each wound taken on the action screen adds +12 × your panic multiplier (at least +6). Since panic makes sutures worse, first treat the wounds that can't fail (bandaging, cleaning) and leave the suture for when the panic goes down. r: The stamp as currency, where it comes from and how it disappears; the mailbox market, the general store and the counter.
x: The stamp is Footfall's currency. It isn't an item that weighs on your backpack: it's a wallet balance . With an online account, the server keeps the balance; your phone collects what you earned and spent and sends it from time to time (each operation only counts once). The balance appears on the BACKPACK tab ( Wallet: N stamp(s) ) and at the top of the mailbox. Where stamps come from Source How many First character kit (1 per device and per account) 10 stamps, along with an Outpost radio Stamp item in loot Lists for shops (including post offices), houses and supply crates (which bring 3 to 6 at once) Common zombie body 6% chance of 1 ("letter in the pocket") Inmate zombie body 35% chance of 1 to 3 Supermarket clerk zombie body 30% chance of 1 to 2 Weekly radio mission 10 stamps Taxes from a stronghold 4 per day, minus the guards' wages Duplicate outfit stored in the wardrobe 2 / 5 / 12 / 30 (common / uncommon / rare / legendary) Duplicate memory book 3 stamps (they come in as an item, so they go through the thermostat below) Sale on the market The agreed price minus the fee Sale at the general store counter About 1/3 of the guide, dropping with each unit Every Stamp item that goes into the backpack, the chests or the depot becomes balance instantly. Stamps from loot go through the server's thermostat : the quantity is multiplied by a factor between 0.6 and 1.4 (it starts at 1), with randomized rounding. The server also caps the wallet's accepted earnings at 1,500 stamps per day. How stamps disappear Drain Rule Death You keep the wallet, but it loses 15% (rounded), which vanishes from the game 300 cap Without spending anything for more than 14 days, the balance above 300 loses 2% of the excess per week (at least 1 per week), never dropping below 300; at most 52 weeks at once Rent Every week: 1 stamp per 100 kg in the radio depot (minimum 1 if there's anything) + 2 per outpost beyond the first Market 1 stamp per offer posted; the fee on each sale General store The price of each item bought Cap example: with 500 idle stamps, the first week takes ⌊200 × 0.02⌋ = 4 (leaving 496), the second ⌊196 × 0.02⌋ = 3, and so on. Spending any stamp restarts the 14-day count. The mailbox The market and general store are at the mailbox , in two places: the one in the radio depot ( MAILBOX: MARKET AND STORE ), which you can reach from any outpost; a mailbox placed at your base (recipe M13: 2 planks + 2 nails). Away from them: "Use the mailbox in the radio vault (from any outpost) or build one at your base." The Mailbox screen has three tabs: Tab What for Needs internet Market Buying and selling with other players, in stamps yes (online account) General store Buying the basics and selling anything at the counter no Value How much your backpack is worth by the price guide no (offline it uses the base price) What you can sell: whatever is loose in the backpack and, at the base, in the chests; inside the depot, also what's in the depot. Market The market is a blind order book: "6 slots. Your offer is matched with someone else's at the price of whoever came first, but nobody sees what others are trading: only the guide price." r: How much you carry in your pockets and backpack, what changes the limit, the effect of a heavy load, belt, back, the pockets-first rule and dropping items on the ground.
x: Everything you carry is in one of two places: your pockets (quick access, at hand during a fight) or the worn backpack (holds more, but taking something out of it mid-fight takes time and makes noise). What is worn or hung on the body weighs nothing. Going over the limit of either one leaves you with a heavy load . Capacity Pockets Pockets = (4 kg + pockets of each worn piece of clothing) × multiplier + 0.5 kg per Strength level. The 4 kg are the body (hands and shallow pockets). Torn clothing counts only half its pockets until it is sewn. Piece Slot Extra pockets Multi-pocket vest Vest 4 kg Tactical vest Vest 3 kg (and unlocks the 3rd belt slot) Cargo pants Pants 3 kg Tactical pants Pants 3 kg Jacket with pockets Clothing 2 kg Windbreaker Clothing 1.5 kg Tactical thigh pouch Leg pouch 1.5 kg Fanny pack Fanny pack 1.5 kg Jeans Pants 1 kg Leather jacket Clothing 1 kg Thick coat Clothing 1 kg Ballistic vest Vest 1 kg Tactical shin pouch Leg pouch 0.8 kg Dark sweatshirt Clothing 0.5 kg Sweatpants Pants 0.5 kg Arm pouch Arm pouch 0.5 kg Since each slot takes only one piece, the maximum pocket space from clothing is: 4 (body) + 4 (multi-pocket vest) + 3 (cargo or tactical pants) + 2 (jacket with pockets) + 1.5 (thigh pouch) + 1.5 (fanny pack) + 0.5 (arm pouch) = 16.5 kg before multipliers. Backpack Backpack = capacity of the worn backpack × multiplier (Strength doesn't add here). Backpack Holds Its weight Rarity Note Gym bag 5 kg 0.4 kg common - School backpack 6 kg 0.5 kg common comes in the starter kit Daypack 10 kg 0.8 kg rare - Tactical backpack 12 kg 1.2 kg rare the MOLLE straps unlock the 3rd belt slot Expedition pack 16 kg 2.0 kg rare 5% slower in combat and +0.015 noise on the map With no backpack worn, only the pockets count. Multiplier (traits) Trait Effect on the limit Strong +20% Organized +30% Weak -20% Disorganized -30% The traits add up (Strong and Organized together give ×1.5) and apply to both pockets and backpack. Strength adds 0.5 kg per level, only to the pockets, after the multiplier. Example Jeans and school backpack, no traits, Strength 0: pockets 4 + 1 = 5 kg; backpack 6 kg; total 11 kg. Heavy load You have a heavy load when the weight in your pockets goes over the pocket limit or the weight in the backpack goes over the backpack limit. The "Heavy load" status appears and the border of the backpack icon turns orange. Situation On the map On the action screen More than 75% of the total used - slower: 1 - 0.4 × (usage - 0.75), up to 10% slower ("Backpack almost full") Heavy load +0.03 noise (about 3.6 m) speed ×0.8 and swings 15% slower ("Backpack too heavy") Expedition pack worn +0.015 noise speed ×0.95 Picking up something that makes you heavy shows "Heavy backpack: slower and noisier.". Nothing stops you from picking it up: what doesn't fit anywhere stays in the backpack (or in your pockets, with no backpack) and you're just heavy. The pockets-first rule A new item is stored automatically: Goes to the pockets first : medicine and dressings (everything in the medical category), ammo, throwables ( molotov , firework , alarm clock , bottle , rock ), batteries and flashlight . If it doesn't fit in the pockets, it goes to the backpack. Everything else goes to the backpack first , and to the pockets if the backpack is full. With no backpack, everything goes to the pockets. When an item is used, it comes out of the pockets first if you're on the action screen, or out of the backpack first if you're on the map (so the pockets always hold what you need in a fight). You can move items between pockets and backpack on the backpack screen ("Does not fit in your pockets.", "Does not fit in the backpack.", "You have no backpack."). r: What happens when your survivor dies: the pile with everything you were carrying, the zombie with your face, the wallet, what stays, the gravestones and the new character.
x: Death in Footfall is permanent for the character: profession, traits and skills are gone. But the world goes on: the base, the chests and most of the wallet stay, and everything you were carrying stays on the ground where you fell, with zombie-you on top of it, waiting for the next survivor to come get it. r: The 14 professions: points, skill levels, free traits and special effects of each one.
x: The profession is the first choice in character creation . It sets how many points you have to spend on traits , gives starting levels in skills and, in some cases, free traits or an effect of its own. The profession doesn't change later: it lasts until the character dies . How to read the points Positive points are left over to buy positive traits. Negative points are a debt: you need to take enough negative traits for the balance to reach 0 or more before starting. The better the profession, the more negative it is. A profession's free traits come already checked, cost no points and can't be removed. They also block the traits that conflict with them (for example, a Personal trainer can't take Asthmatic, because they already have Athletic). The skill levels given by the profession add up with those from traits such as Handyman and First responder, capped at level 10. r: How to loot through the door or from inside, the time and noise of each piece of furniture, how many items you get, the rarity roll, ultra-rare finds, weekly restocking, locked doors and glass cuts.
x: Looting means opening furniture in real places on the map (pharmacies, markets, police stations, houses...) to find items. Each piece of furniture takes time and makes noise. The more you've walked in the session, and the deeper you go into the place, the better the chance of something rare. What you take is gone for the other survivors until the place restocks. Where you can loot The map's Loot button searches within 35 m of you (the GPS margin): places on the map (shops, services; see the types in Health , Market , Restaurant , Construction , Gas station , Police , Fire station , School , Clothes , Electronics , Shop ); houses : any building of 20 to 600 m² with no shop, with you within 12 m of the wall; bodies of killed zombies and items dropped on the ground (bodies take priority when everything is close); supply drops and rescue crates (see Horde and alarms ); the month's bunkers . With only one thing nearby, it opens directly. With more than one, the Loot list appears (up to 8, from nearest to farthest), and places already looted show "already looted (you can enter)". With nothing: "Nothing to loot nearby". Through the door or going inside A place's loot screen shows two options side by side: Through the door Enter Where on the loot screen itself, on the map opens the action screen outside the main door, with the building's interior Furniture the 3 ground-floor pieces closest to the main door all the others, on every floor Rares never (rarity multiplier 0) multiplier 1.5 (in the bunker, higher on each floor) Ultra-rare finds no yes (see below) Danger only the street zombies the zombies inside, plus those outside who hear the noise Buildings 9 m tall or more have 2 floors, 12 m or more have 3; schools, police stations and fire stations always have at least 2; houses have 2 at 6 m or more. Upper floors have fewer zombies (60%). You can also go inside by walking on the action screen: getting within 3.5 m of a place's door opens it from the inside on its own; outside free-walk mode the ENTER: place name button appears. Rummaging On the loot screen, tap Rummage (X s · noise) on a piece of furniture. On the action screen, get within 1.3 m of it and tap RUMMAGE FURNITURE NAME . Stay still until the bar fills. One piece of furniture at a time. Once it's open: tap an item to take it (ammo comes as the whole stack) or tap Take all . Time = furniture time ÷ (looting speed). The Burglar profession loots 1.5× faster; being sad (sadness level 2 or more) makes it 10% slower. Interruptions : On the map, moving more than 20 m from the point where you opened the loot cancels it ("Looting interrupted: you moved away."). If the action screen starts (a zombie saw you), the loot closes ("Looting interrupted!") and reopens on its own when the fight ends, if you're still within 35 m. On the action screen, moving more than 0.45 m, being knocked down or being grabbed stops the search ("Stopped rummaging."). Opening the first piece of furniture marks the place as looted for 7 days (the bunker, until the start of the next month). A looted place can still be opened: whatever's left is still there. Glass cuts Each piece of furniture you open (bodies don't count) has a 4% chance of you cutting your hand on a shard: a shard is left in your hand ("You cut your hand on a shard of glass: there's a shard in it. Check the Health screen."). Time and noise of each piece of furniture Noise is the level from 0 to 1 while you rummage; the radius is noise × 120 m (before rain). See Noise . r: How to start and end a session, what each map button does, the compass and the GPS rules.
x: In Footfall you play by actually walking. Everything that happens on the map (zombies moving, looting, distance traveled, noise) only runs while a session is open. Outside a session the character is "sleeping" or "standing still" where you ended, and only real time passes (hunger, thirst, fatigue, healing). Starting a session Have a character created. Without one, the map shows Create character and starting is refused with "Create a character before you start.". Tap START SESSION at the bottom of the map. The game checks whether the device's location is on ("GPS off. Turn on your device's location.") and whether permission was granted ("Location permission denied."). It asks for your current position for up to 12 s . If the GPS doesn't respond, it uses the last known position and corrects it later. Without either, "Couldn't get your GPS position. Go somewhere open and tap again." appears. The whole attempt has a 30 s limit. Past that: "The GPS took too long to respond. Go somewhere open and tap again.". Tapping twice doesn't open two sessions. When it starts, the game: applies the rest from the time the app was closed (see Sleeping or ending ); resets the session distance (it's used for the rare item chance, see Looting ); checks the month (zombies come back every month, see Zombies ), the night attacks on the base and the weekly horde ; schedules the first random alarm for 8 to 11 minutes from now; loads the streets and places around you (first 500 m, to start quickly, then 1,400 m) and fetches the real weather . The map is downloaded within a 1,400 m radius. When you get more than 550 m from the center of the downloaded chunk (and enter another chunk), the game downloads the new chunk on its own. If the internet fails, it tries again after 5, 15, 30, 60, 120 and then every 300 s; the notice at the top shows the countdown and tapping it retries right away. Delivery driver profession In the first session, the delivery driver already starts with about 400 m around them marked on the explored map ("You know this neighborhood well: it's already on your map."). The start message in the log is "Session started. You can be attacked.": from here on the zombies on the map can see, hear and chase you. Sleeping or ending To finish, open the Menu (three-dot icon in the left corner) and choose: Sleep (end here) , when you're somewhere safe: inside the base, at an outpost or at the tent camp. End session , anywhere else ("Outside the base: poor rest, without losing anything."). A window confirms ( Sleep / End or Keep playing ). Ending anywhere keeps everything you're carrying. The difference is in the rest while the app stays closed: Where you ended Rest rate Health per hour closed Mind (stress, sadness) Base, with a bed placed 18.75 (the best) +7.5 counts 1.5× the hours Base without a bed, outpost or tent 12.5 +5 counts the normal hours Outside, with a sleeping bag in the backpack 8 +2.5 counts 1.2× the hours Outside, on the ground 4 nothing counts the normal hours Health only comes back while sleeping if you're not bleeding or infected. Hunger and thirst keep running in any case. Ending also turns off the flashlight, closes any open loot and the action screen. The menu's Home screen button is locked during the session ("End the session first."). r: When the action screen starts, the safe-spot confirmation, the arena radius, the zombie cap, the grace periods, where there's no fighting and how to leave.
x: The action screen is where fighting happens: a top-down scene built from the real streets, buildings, cars and furniture around you, plus every zombie in range. On it you move with the joystick (not with GPS), fight, search places from the inside and search bodies. When it starts On its own If a zombie that is chasing you gets within 25 m of you on the map, the action screen opens on its own. This doesn't happen: during a grace period (see below); inside the base with the walls standing (closed base); during the avenue pause ("Cross carefully — threat paused", see Session and map ). With the button The big fight button on the map opens the action screen immediately, anywhere. Anyone who hasn't seen you starts unaware : you can sneak up from behind. Other ways in Enter a place from the loot screen (see Looting ). Go to the base through an outpost or the tent. The radio vault and the arena of a held point also use the action screen. Confirmation: "THEY'RE HERE" When the fight started on its own, before the scene a warning screen appears with the number of zombies in range: "Before fighting, stop somewhere safe: on the sidewalk, away from the street, not crossing anything. The fight will wait for you." The fight doesn't advance while it's open. Tap I'M STILL AND SAFE · FIGHT to start. With this screen or the action screen open, walking in real life doesn't count distance (neither for rares nor for missions). The arena Rule Value Scene radius 120 m around where you were Zombies that come in all of those on the map within 120 m, nearest to farthest, up to 40 Those already chasing you or that had half-noticed you start alert Fallen ones lying on the map start lying down (unaware ones stay on the ground until they notice you) The scene starts with you facing where you were facing on the map. If the GPS put you inside a building, you start on the nearest street. At the start, notes on what weighs on this fight appear for a few seconds: hunger, thirst, fatigue, pain, fracture, illness, load, night, fog, rain, stress, medicine. Free roam The regular action screen, opened on the street (by button or on its own), is free roam : past 40 m from the center, the scene restarts around you: the terrain is rebuilt, new zombies in range come in (up to 40 in the scene) and those left far away leave; you can only step where your explored map already covers (the rest stays dark), at the base and in its yard; getting within 3.5 m of a place's door opens it from the inside right there; leaving and moving 6 m from the door closes it again; there's no escape edge. In the other scenes (place opened with Enter , base through the outpost) there's a red edge at 120 m: crossing it is escaping. Places without fighting Closed base : inside the base with the walls standing, map zombies stop chasing you and forget the noise they heard, and fights don't start on their own. The streets inside it are blocked to them. Avenues : during the crossing pause, zombies stop completely. Radio vault and arena : no map zombie gets in. Bunker safe rooms : the armored door doesn't let zombies through (see Bunkers ). r: Feels-like temperature from the real weather, clothes that warm and weigh you down, cold and heat levels and what they cost.
x: Footfall uses the real weather in your area. Temperature, rain, fog and thunderstorms come from a weather service based on your rounded position (about 1 km) and are updated every 30 minutes. Without internet, the game keeps the last reading; if it never managed to get one, there are no temperature effects. The Backpack tab shows the current temperature ("Now N °C") and warns when you're missing warm clothes or wearing too many heavy ones. Feels-like temperature For cold , the game uses the feels-like temperature: feels like = temperature − 4 (if it's raining and you're not protected) − 2 (if it's night) Rain : subtracts 4 °C, unless you're wearing a Raincoat or Windbreaker . Night : subtracts 2 °C. Night runs from sunset to sunrise, calculated from your position and date. Wind : doesn't factor in. Real wind changes the ambient sound and, above 30 km/h, wears out the tarp of a pitched tent faster. For heat , the game uses the real temperature, with no deductions, and only during the day. Cold First the game checks how much warm clothing the feels-like temperature calls for: Feels-like temperature Calls for 16 °C or more 0 warmth 10 °C to 15.9 °C 1 warmth Below 10 °C 2 warmth Then it subtracts the warmth of the clothes you're wearing (torn pieces don't keep you warm): Clothing Warmth Thick coat 2 Leather jacket 1 Jacket with pockets 1 Dark sweatshirt 1 Beanie 1 What's missing is the cold level (0 to 2). Example: 8 °C at night in the rain gives a feels-like of 2 °C, which calls for 2; in a sweatshirt (1), cold 1 remains. A coat and a beanie together add up to 3, enough for any temperature. There's no cold: inside the base; outside a session; for 3 h after having a Hot soup . Heat Heat depends on the real temperature and the load of heavy clothing worn: Heavy clothing Load Thick coat 2 Leather jacket 1 Jacket with pockets 1 Ballistic vest 1 Tactical vest 1 Ballistic helmet 1 Tactical helmet with light 1 Firefighter helmet 1 Expedition pack 1 Temperature Load 0 Load 1 Load 2 or more 28 °C or less 0 0 0 Above 28 °C up to 33 °C 0 1 2 Above 33 °C 1 2 2 The Cap removes 1 from the heat level. Above 33 °C, even without heavy clothing, you feel heat 1, unless you're wearing a cap. There's no heat at night. Unlike cold, heat also applies inside the base (but only with the session active). Torn pieces still weigh you down. Effects Level Cold Heat 1 Cold: −8 max stamina; +14.4 kcal burned per hour Hot: −8 max stamina; +43.2 ml of water used per hour 2 Freezing: −16 max stamina; +28.8 kcal per hour Boiling: −16 max stamina; +86.4 ml per hour The stamina penalty applies before the trait multipliers (see Traits ). The extra consumption comes out of your hunger and thirst reserves and only runs with the session active, on the map. Rain, fog and storms Besides the feels-like temperature, the weather changes other things that aren't temperature: rain reduces your vision and muffles your noise, fog greatly reduces vision and thunder muffles footsteps. These effects are covered in Weather and time , Vision and Noise . Dress for the forecast On a cold, rainy day, the raincoat alone already cancels the rain's 4 °C. On a hot day, swap the coat for the sweatshirt or the jacket and put on the cap: the coat alone is already load 2.

r: Every first aid step: time, accepted items, failure chance, the quick dressing and how to speed up healing.
x: Every wound is treated step by step on the Health tab of the character panel. Each wound shows only the steps still missing, in the right order to do them. It only heals once all steps are done and there's no infection. Treating gives First aid XP, and the skill level makes each step faster and safer. Where to treat On the map : open the character panel (heart icon, Character ) and go to the Health tab. The Vitruvian figure at the top shows the state of each body part; tapping a part highlights it. Below are the bars (Health, Hunger, Thirst, Fatigue, Stress, Sadness, Boredom, Pain) and one card per wound. On the action screen : the same panel opens straight to the Health tab when you're hurt. You can also treat yourself in the middle of a fight. On the base stretcher : tapping the stretcher on the action screen opens Health and reminds you that wounds heal faster there. When you can't treat On the map, no step can be done with a zombie chasing you: "There's a zombie after you. Get away first.". On the action screen, the block is any zombie within 6 m: "A zombie is too close. Move a few meters away to treat yourself.". How a step works On the wound card, each missing step is a button with the step's name and, below it, the item that will be used (or in hand , or missing <item> if you have none; then the button is disabled). Tapping it opens a window with the step's name, the item used, warnings ("It is at the bottom of the backpack: finding it takes longer.", "Chance to fail: N% (level and panic count).") and a bar with the seconds remaining. You can tap Stop to give up before the bar fills; nothing is used up. When the bar fills, the item is used up and the step is done (or fails). The result appears, for example "Bandage (with Gauze): done.". The item is looked for in the backpack and, if you're at the base, in the chests. On the action screen, the game prefers what's in your pockets; if the item is only at the bottom of the backpack, the step takes 2.5 s longer. With cachaça, the Empty bottle is left over. Remove the shrapnel : with tweezers, the tweezers aren't used up. Without tweezers, it's done by hand: the step is still possible ("No tweezers: done by hand (it hurts and bleeds).") and takes 3 health. Suture : uses 1 suture kit per attempt. Closes the deep cut and the hemorrhage; on a hemorrhage, it also releases the tourniquet. Bandage : with a Sterile dressing or a First aid kit, the wound also counts as clean. With a rag, the dressing starts out dirty. If you have Medical tape , it's used up along with it and the dressing takes 24 h instead of 12 h to get dirty. When the dressing gets dirty, the button comes back as Change dressing . Tourniquet : stops the hemorrhage instantly. Don't go more than 2 h without a suture: after that it takes 1 HP every 120 s. Immobilize (splint) : the only step for a fracture. The splint is made with 1 plank and 2 rags. Ointment : first step for a burn; bandage it afterwards. r: The vision cone on the map and on the action screen, day and night ranges, flashlight, binoculars, weather, walls and woods, and how zombies see you.
x: In Footfall you don't see the whole map: you only spot zombies inside a cone in front of you , up to a distance that changes with the time of day, the weather, the flashlight and your traits. Walls block vision and dense woods shorten it. Zombies also have a cone, a smaller one, and only see you inside it. This page explains both sides. Your cone on the map A zombie appears on the map when any of these is true: it is within 6 m of you, in any direction (sound and smell). With binoculars this radius drops to 2 m; or it is inside the cone, within the current range, and no wall blocks the line to it.
