This doesn't apply to binoculars, which always stay at 28°. Range multipliers After the base value from the table, the range is multiplied by everything that applies (in sequence): Factor Multiplier Eagle eyes trait ×1.3 Nearsighted trait ×0.7 Storm ×0.85 Watchtower: base with a placed tower and you less than 40 m from the base ×1.5 Scout role in the group ×1.05 Rain ×0.75 Fog ×0.6 Infection in the delirium stage ×0.6 Example: at night, with a flashlight, in the rain: 90 × 0.75 = 67.5 m in a 60° cone. Walls and woods The game casts 360 rays from you. Each ray stops at the first building wall. The building you're in right now is ignored (GPS sometimes puts you inside a house). Dense woods (the map's vegetation areas) don't stop vision, but each meter inside them costs 4 m of range. With 120 m of range, 30 m of woods is enough to end vision in that direction. What you see gets marked on the explored map (the Map panel). Jump scare A zombie that suddenly appears less than 15 m away adds up to 6 points of panic (more the closer it is). With vibration on, the phone gives a buzz when a new zombie enters your vision. Flashlight You need a flashlight in the backpack, or a helmet with a light being worn ( miner helmet , tactical helmet or headlamp ), and batteries . The button only appears at night, and the flashlight turns itself off when day breaks. It uses 1 battery every 20 min it's on (30 min with a headlamp or helmet). Without batteries it goes out ("The batteries ran out."). It changes your cone to 60° and 90 m (see the table above). It gives you away: with the flashlight on, zombies see you at 30 m instead of 8 m. On top of that, every 3 s, every zombie within 50 m with a clear line to you (and that isn't lying down or already chasing you) wakes up and heads to where you are. On the action screen, a handheld flashlight that's only at the bottom of the backpack has to be dug out first (2.5 s; see Backpack and weight ). r: How zombies live on the map (dormant, wandering and downed), how they notice and chase you, where they spawn, when they come back and every uniform type with its multipliers.
x: The city has a fixed population of zombies: each stretch of street has its own, always the same ones during the month, and every phone sees the same zombies in the same place. Some died in uniform (police officers, doctors, soldiers...) and are tougher and carry job-specific loot. The three states on the map State Chance Behavior Dormant 65% standing still, eyes half closed. Sees and hears at half strength until it notices something. At night, 3 in every 8 get up and roam (6 in 8 on a full moon) Wandering 25% walks a little along the streets near home and stops for a while (by day it rests 20 to 60 s, at night 8 to 25 s, in a storm half that); each walk lasts 5 to 15 s Downed 10% lying down like a corpse. It doesn't see; it only hears up close (30% of the radius). It only gets up when it hears something or when a fight starts near it Zombies move along the streets (the map's street graph). Near you, when chasing, they leave the street and come straight at you (within 20 m, or when they're on the same stretch of street). When roaming, none of them strays more than 40 m from the spot where it lives; if it does, it comes back. Speed on the map m/s Chasing 1.2 (a bit slower than you walking) Following a sound 1.08 Drawn by an alarm 0.96 Roaming 0.4 In the small hours they all move 15% faster. On the map, speed doesn't change with the uniform; only on the action screen. How they notice you Sight : a 100° cone in the direction it's looking, 15 m by day, 8 m at night, 30 m if your flashlight is on. It notices you gradually: 1 s up close, 2 s at the edge. Details in Vision . Hearing : radius = noise × 120 m. Within 8 m it comes right away; within 100 m it goes to the sound. Details in Noise . Neighbors : one that has seen you makes all others within 20 m of it start chasing too. Only zombies within 150 m of you "think" (move and notice). Those more than 750 m away leave memory and remember where they were. Chasing and giving up When chasing, it takes the shortest street path to you. If it gets within 25 m, the action screen starts. If it goes 15 s without seeing or hearing you (and is more than 20 m away), it loses the trail and goes to the last place it saw you. There, it searches for 8 s , looking around. Then dormant and downed ones go back to sleep; wandering ones go back to roaming. More than 450 m from you it gives up immediately. Inside a closed base, they all give up and forget the sound. A zombie that was drawn somewhere else (by an alarm, a sound or a chase) starts living where it ended up. Where they spawn and how many The city is divided into cells of about 100 × 100 m. Each cell has: Cell Zombies With loot places 10 + 4 per place "guard" + 0 to 4, between 5 and 30. Each place counts by its type's number of guards (Health, Market and Police 3; Restaurant, Construction, Outpost, Fire station and School 2; the others 1) No places, in a green area 5 No places, ordinary street 6 to 10 Within the cell, street points within 40 m of a loot place are 4× more likely to get a zombie. No one spawns inside your base. The population is generated within 500 m of you. Inside places there are other zombies, which depend on the place's type and size; those come back every week (see Looting ). When they come back Once killed on the map, a zombie doesn't come back until the month turns over. In the new month they all come back ("New month: the zombies are back."), with the same distribution for everyone. Zombies inside places come back every week; bunker zombies come back on every visit. Uniform types A zombie's health on the action screen is 12 to 20, and its speed 0.9 to 1.35, both multiplied by the uniform.
